newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds well supported, market awaits jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds well supported, market awaits jobs data.

text.p: German debt prices started off on a firm footing on Tuesday although early volumes were thin after a bank holiday weekend in Britain and ahead of German April jobless data.

The impact on German fixed income markets of the unemployment data is likely to be limited, with leaked figures already in the market and suggesting a 130,000 non-adjusted fall on the month. Analysts said that this would roughly translate into a seasonally-adjusted fall of around 5,000.
By 0631, the DTB June future was trading eight basis points higher on the day at 101.84, off its earlier 101.90 high.
With the jobless fall likely to be smaller than expected, traders said the outlook for steady German interest rates would be reinforced, supporting the Bund market in the medium term.
But the market might suffer from external influences, with nerves sharpening ahead of French elections and what the outome might mean for Europe's planned single currency.

Bunds' fragility in the face of European hiccups was already being reflected in the 10-year yield spread of cash German paper to Treasuries, which had snapped in to 100 basis points early on Tuesday from around 106 late last week.

In the short term, analysts said the DTB Bund future would find key support at 101.61, a Fibonacci retracement level which the market overcame on the way up late last week. On the upside, the critical target is now at 102.00, they said.
"A push above 102.00 would likely provide further support to prices to argue for 102.18, 102.35 and then 102.46," one analysts said in a morning note.
He said investors whould remain optimistic for the the near term, buying on any dips towards to the 101.62 level.
In cooperation with the German association for materials management, purschasing and logistics, Reuters will present the new German Purchasing Managers' Index for the first time at 0800 GMT.

The indicator, which is closely modelled on the U.S. National Asssociation of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index, is based on a survey of 350 companies and will give a view of overall activity in the manufacturing economy.
